staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 preserved the vulnerable libxml2 checkout used for reproduction. Its line map matches the saved ASan frames at `SAX2.c:1247`, `tree.c:837`, `xinclude.c:1987`, `xinclude.c:2232`, and `xmlsave.c:897`.

classification.classification_note: The saved `fuzz/xml` run records an 8-byte heap use-after-free read in `xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal` while serializing a document after XInclude processing. Source analysis and the fix diff show that fallback handling stores `fallback->children` directly in `incTab[nr]->inc` instead of copying the list, so later XInclude replacement frees namespace-owning nodes while another document-reachable node still retains `cur->ns` pointing at the same `xmlNs`. The witness free stack specifically leaves through `xmlFreeNode(cur)` at `xinclude.c:2232`.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal (xmlsave.c): during XInclude processing (xmlXIncludeIncludeNode in xinclude.c) namespace/node structures are freed (via xmlFreeNs/xmlFreeNode) while they are still reachable and later accessed by document-dumping functions (xmlDocContentDumpOutput / xmlDocDumpFormatMemoryEnc). This use-after-free can cause crashes and memory corruption, with potential for exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: The witness drives `fuzz/xml` down the pull-parser branch with `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` enabled. The decoded XML entity contains an `xi:include` element with an `xi:fallback` subtree, and parsing that subtree allocates an `xmlNs` object for its namespace declaration. When the include target load fails, `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback()` stores `fallback->children` directly in `ctxt->incTab[nr]->inc` instead of copying them. That leaves XInclude replacement operating on original fallback nodes rather than an independent replacement list. The saved AddressSanitizer stack shows the crashing namespace object being released when `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` takes the `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` branch, inserts the aliased replacement list, unlinks the original include node, and frees it with `xmlFreeNode(cur)` at `xinclude.c:2232`; `xmlFreeNode()` then frees a namespace list through `xmlFreeNsList()` and `xmlFreeNs()`. Because fallback children were not copied or namespace-fixed before this ownership-changing replacement, a document-reachable node later still carries `cur->ns` pointing at that freed `xmlNs`. When `xmlDocDumpFormatMemoryEnc()` serializes the document, `xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal()` reads `cur->ns->prefix` and triggers the recorded heap-use-after-free. The patch fixes the ownership failure by copying fallback children with `xmlDocCopyNodeList()` and by moving fallback-child removal earlier in the other replacement branch.

source.description: First project-side materialization of attacker-controlled state on the witnessed path. This statement reads the fuzz container's option word that later enables XInclude processing in the pull-parser serializer path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with bytes `ff ff ff 20`, so this statement copies little-endian `0x20ffff` into `ret`. After `opts &= ~XML_PARSE_HUGE` in `fuzz/xml.c:38`, the resulting flags still satisfy `opts & XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE`, which is the gate used at `fuzz/xml.c:50` before `xmlXIncludeProcessFlags(doc, opts)`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Crash sink. The serializer reaches a document node whose `cur->ns` pointer still references a freed namespace object and reads `cur->ns->prefix`.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace records `READ of size 8` at `xmlsave.c:897:48` in this conditional.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. Vulnerable fallback handling retains the original fallback child list instead of copying it, so later XInclude replacement reuses nodes whose namespace ownership still belongs to the fallback subtree and can free shared namespace state while a document-reachable node still references it.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this assignment to `xmlDocCopyNodeList(ctxt->doc, fallback->children)`, showing that the missing obligation is to break aliasing between replacement content and the original fallback subtree before replacement frees or restructures nodes.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific XML admission gate. After the fuzz container is decoded, the main entity must still begin with `<` so libxml2 enters normal element parsing instead of rejecting the document as empty.

tainted_value_origin.description: Container-retained stale-alias origin. The include table keeps a pointer to the original fallback child list rather than an independent copy, so later replacement code acts on nodes whose namespace ownership was not detached from the fallback subtree.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first four witness bytes are materialized as the parser option word. On this sample the resulting flags still satisfy the later `opts & XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` gate used before XInclude processing.

The same fuzz container is decoded into the main XML entity consumed by `xmlReadMemory`. The staged witness begins with `<xi:include href="a" xmlns:xi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude"><xi:fallback><xi:i`, so it provides the include/fallback structure that drives the vulnerable path.

While parsing the fallback subtree, libxml2 allocates and attaches an `xmlNs` object for the attacker-controlled namespace declaration. ASan's allocation stack records this namespace allocation as the object later freed and reused.

fine_trace.code:
xmlXIncludeSetFlags(ctxt, flags);
ret = xmlXIncludeDoProcess(ctxt, tree->doc, tree, 0);
fine_trace.note: XInclude processing copies the attacker-derived flags into the XInclude context and starts include resolution on the parsed document. The fallback path is reachable only because this call executes when `opts & XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` is true in the fuzz target.

Root cause. After include loading fails and fallback processing is selected, libxml2 stores the original fallback child list directly in the include table. The replacement list therefore aliases original fallback nodes instead of an independent copy.

The saved free stack's branch. With `ctxt->parseFlags & XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` set, XInclude inserts the aliased replacement list before the original include node, then unlinks and frees that original node through `xmlFreeNode(cur)` at `xinclude.c:2232`.

fine_trace.code:
if (((cur->type == XML_ELEMENT_NODE) ||
     (cur->type == XML_XINCLUDE_START) ||
     (cur->type == XML_XINCLUDE_END)) &&
    (cur->nsDef != NULL))
    xmlFreeNsList(cur->nsDef);
fine_trace.note: Freeing the original include-side node releases its namespace-definition list. The saved ASan free stack continues from here through `xmlFreeNsList()` and `xmlFreeNs()`, confirming that the namespace object allocated in step 3 is deallocated during `xmlFreeNode(cur)`.

Later serialization walks the document after XInclude processing and dispatches a still-linked node from the replacement result into `xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal`. That node remains document-reachable after step 6 even though shared namespace state was freed in step 7.
Sink. The serializer reads `cur->ns->prefix` from a node whose `cur->ns` still references the namespace freed in step 7, producing the recorded heap-use-after-free read.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Patch and source analysis tie the serializer UAF to fallback-child aliasing at `xinclude.c:1987`; the allocation context is the namespace created for the fallback subtree at `SAX2.c:1247`, and the saved free stack shows that shared namespace state is released during `xmlFreeNode(cur)` at `xinclude.c:2232`.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz/xml container with one XML main entity
format.contract: The witness must encode parser options whose post-mask value still satisfies `opts & XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE`. Its first entity must start with `<` and contain an `xi:include` element with an `xi:fallback` subtree so fallback processing runs when the include target fails to load. The same options must also leave `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` set so the witnessed `xmlFreeNode(cur)` branch at `xinclude.c:2232` executes before serialization reaches a node that still reads the freed namespace through `cur->ns->prefix`.
